questions.question: Shifting gears while turning:

options.text: Should only be done if you can do it smoothly.
Is better than shifting before the turn.
Is the best way to control your speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should only be done if you can do it smoothly.
questions.explanation: It is best to shift gears before you start a turn. If you must shift while turning, do it smoothly. A sudden change in power to the rear wheel can cause a skid.

questions.question: Hearing protection:

options.text: Is not needed when wearing a helmet.
Is only recommended for long trips.
Should be used on every ride.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be used on every ride.
questions.explanation: Engine and wind noise can damage your hearing, even with a helmet on. Wear hearing protection on every ride.

questions.question: As your motorcycle speeds up, you will:

options.text: Need to shift to higher gears.
Need to shift to lower gears.
Need to put the motorcycle in neutral.

questions.correctAnswerText: Need to shift to higher gears.
questions.explanation: You must shift into higher gears as your motorcycle goes faster.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop.
Yield to other drivers.
A stop sign is coming up.

questions.correctAnswerText: A stop sign is coming up.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns you that a stop sign is coming up.

questions.question: The best way to stay safe while riding is to:

options.text: Look far ahead on the road.
Avoid areas with heavy traffic.
Ride faster than the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look far ahead on the road.
questions.explanation: Watch the road ahead to spot dangers before you reach them. This helps you avoid problems while riding.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, moving to the far side of your lane:

options.text: Is a good idea because you will be farther from the passing vehicle.
Is not a good idea because it may make the other driver move back into your lane too soon.
Does not affect safety either way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is not a good idea because it may make the other driver move back into your lane too soon.
questions.explanation: Do not move to the far side of your lane when being passed. This may cause the passing driver to return to your lane too soon.

questions.question: In California, drivers under 21 cannot operate a vehicle with a blood alcohol content (BAC) of:

options.text: 0.01 percent or higher.
0.08 percent or higher.
0.1 percent or higher.

questions.correctAnswerText: 0.01 percent or higher.
questions.explanation: In California, you must be 21 to drink alcohol. Drivers under 21 cannot ride with a BAC of 0.01 percent or higher. Even small amounts of alcohol can make it unsafe to ride a motorcycle.

questions.question: When you must react to a hazard, do not:

options.text: Let other drivers know you are there.
Change your speed.
Use your horn, lights, or signals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let other drivers know you are there.
questions.explanation: Always tell other drivers you are there by using your horn, lights, and signals. Change your speed and position as needed to stay safe.

questions.question: Avoid riding directly next to another vehicle because:

options.text: Another driver may want to use your lane to pass.
You may be hidden in the vehicle's blind spot.
You may have access to escape routes.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be hidden in the vehicle's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding next to another vehicle is dangerous because the driver may not see you in their blind spot. The vehicle could also block your way to escape if a hazard appears.

questions.question: Which factor does NOT greatly affect your blood alcohol content (BAC)?

options.text: Age
The amount of alcohol consumed
Body weight

questions.correctAnswerText: Age
questions.explanation: The main factors that affect BAC are the amount of alcohol consumed, how fast you drink it, and your body weight.

questions.question: You should flash your brake light to:

options.text: Tell other drivers you are riding near them.
Help other drivers see your motorcycle in slow traffic.
Warn other drivers you are slowing down or stopping where they do not expect it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warn other drivers you are slowing down or stopping where they do not expect it.
questions.explanation: Flash your brake light to warn other drivers when you slow down or stop unexpectedly. This is especially important before making tight turns on high-speed roads or slowing down in places where drivers may not expect it.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Yield
Slow-moving vehicle
Railroad crossing

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow-moving vehicle
questions.explanation: This sign is put on the back of slow vehicles that travel under 25 mph. These include farm equipment, construction vehicles, and horse-drawn wagons.

questions.question: When the lights on this sign are flashing, what should you do?

options.text: Stop and wait until the train passes.
Go ahead slowly.
Turn around and find another route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait until the train passes.
questions.explanation: When you see flashing lights at a railroad crossing, stop completely. Wait until the train passes and the lights stop flashing before you go. Never try to beat a train across the tracks.

questions.question: On a motorcycle, which brake provides the most stopping power?

options.text: The front brake
The rear brake
The emergency brake

questions.correctAnswerText: The front brake
questions.explanation: The front brake gives about three-quarters of your motorcycle's stopping power. Use both brakes together every time you stop.

questions.question: When it starts to rain, it is usually best to:

options.text: Ride on the right side of the lane.
Ride on the edge of the road.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: Rain mixes with oil on the road, making it very slippery. Ride in the tire tracks left by cars ahead of you. These tracks are cleaner and have better grip.

questions.question: If the front wheel locks, you should:

options.text: Release the front brake right away, then apply it again.
Release the front brake and use only the rear brake.
Keep the front wheel locked until you stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake right away, then apply it again.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks while braking, let go of the brake immediately. Then apply it again.

questions.question: A motorcycle can have no more than:

options.text: Two wheels.
Three wheels.
Four wheels.

questions.correctAnswerText: Three wheels.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle is a motor vehicle with a seat for the rider and no more than three wheels.

questions.question: If you will be carrying a passenger on your motorcycle, you will likely have to:

options.text: Lower the tire pressure.
Make no tire pressure changes.
Raise the tire pressure.

questions.correctAnswerText: Raise the tire pressure.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight to your motorcycle. Add a few pounds of air pressure to your tires before riding with a passenger. Check your owner's manual for the correct tire pressure.

questions.question: Where is the greatest potential for conflict between you and other vehicles?

options.text: At intersections
On the highway
On any road

questions.correctAnswerText: At intersections
questions.explanation: Most conflicts happen at intersections. The biggest danger is when oncoming cars turn left in front of motorcycles.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Right lane ends
Left lane ends
Traffic control device ahead

questions.correctAnswerText: Right lane ends
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. They tell you about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that the right lane will end.

questions.question: To get the most protection from your helmet, what is most important?

options.text: It fits snugly.
It is clean.
It looks cool.

questions.correctAnswerText: It fits snugly.
questions.explanation: A helmet protects you best when it meets DOT and state standards, fits snugly all around, and has no damage.

questions.question: When approaching an intersection, a motorcyclist should NOT:

options.text: Choose a lane position that makes them more visible.
Speed up to cross the intersection quickly.
Have both hands ready on the clutch and brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up to cross the intersection quickly.
questions.explanation: Slow down as you approach an intersection. Choose a lane position where other drivers can see you. Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes. Do not change speed or position suddenly, as this confuses other drivers.

questions.question: Why should a motorcyclist change gears before starting a turn?

options.text: To prevent a sudden change in power during the turn.
To keep both hands on the handlebars during the turn.
To prevent the motorcycle from slowing down.

questions.correctAnswerText: To prevent a sudden change in power during the turn.
questions.explanation: Change gears before you start a turn. Shifting gears while turning can cause a sudden power change that makes the rear wheel skid. If you must shift while turning, do it smoothly to avoid skidding.

questions.question: What is true about blind spots on motorcycles?

options.text: They are not a concern.
Riders should check them regularly.
They do not exist if the motorcycle has a mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riders should check them regularly.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots just like other vehicles. Always turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes. Make head checks part of your normal riding routine.

questions.question: To avoid confusing other drivers, you should:

options.text: Increase your following distance.
Turn off your turn signal after completing a turn or lane change.
Use your horn only in emergencies.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off your turn signal after completing a turn or lane change.
questions.explanation: Turn off your signal as soon as you finish turning or changing lanes. Leaving it on confuses other drivers about your next move.

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks up while stopping on a straight road, what happens?

options.text: You can usually stay in control.
You will likely lose control.
You must release the rear brake to regain control.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can usually stay in control.
questions.explanation: If your rear wheel locks during a straight stop, keep it locked until you stop. You can usually control your motorcycle even with a locked rear wheel if it stays upright and travels straight.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The traffic light is about to turn red.
The traffic light is about to turn green.
Stop and wait for traffic to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: The traffic light is about to turn red.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow light warns that the light will turn red soon. Slow down and stop before the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are already in the intersection when it turns yellow, keep going through.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Signal ahead
Crossroad ahead
Divided roadway ahead

questions.correctAnswerText: Divided roadway ahead
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that the road is divided.

questions.question: On a highway, a motorcyclist should signal before changing lanes for:

options.text: Two seconds
Five seconds
10 seconds

questions.correctAnswerText: Five seconds
questions.explanation: Signal a lane change at least five seconds before you move. This gives other drivers time to react safely.

questions.question: When approaching a blind intersection, riders should:

options.text: Stop at the stop line, then move forward to see cross traffic better.
Ignore the stop line and move forward to see better.
Stop at the stop line then proceed through.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop at the stop line, then move forward to see cross traffic better.
questions.explanation: Stop at the stop line first. Then move forward slowly and stop again just before the crossroad. Lean forward to look around buildings, parked cars, or bushes for approaching traffic. Keep your front wheel out of the crossroad while looking.
